name: Notta
tagline: Transcribe uploaded or live audio, summarize it, and organize a personal archive

pricing.basis: annual billing, per user per month
pricing.notes: Advertised annual-equivalent price; monthly billing is higher.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 seat; 120 transcription minutes/month; 3 minutes per recording; 50 uploads, 10 AI summaries, 1,000 Brain credits, 4 bilingual uses, and 2 monolingual translation uses per month.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 1 seat; 1,800 transcription minutes/month; 5 hours per recording; 100 uploads, 100 AI summaries, 1,000 Brain credits, and 200 vocabulary terms per month/account.
tiers.notes: Annual equivalent verified; monthly numeric price was not exposed by the live rendered page.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited transcription; 5 hours per recording; 200 uploads, 200 AI summaries, 1,000 Brain credits, and 1,000 vocabulary terms per account/month.
tiers.notes: Annual equivalent verified; monthly numeric price was not exposed by the live rendered page.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Starts at 51 seats; customized transcription; 5 hours per recording; unlimited uploads, AI summaries, and vocabulary.

tiers.name: Monolingual Translation add-on
tiers.limits: Up to 100 translation uses per account/month on Pro or Business; unlimited on Enterprise.
tiers.notes: Monthly price verified; annual-billing equivalent was not exposed.

tiers.name: Bilingual Transcription & Translation add-on
tiers.limits: Up to 200 uses per account/month on Pro or Business; unlimited on Enterprise.
tiers.notes: Monthly price verified; annual-billing equivalent was not exposed.

tiers.name: Notta Brain add-on
tiers.notes: Public numeric price was not exposed.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 seat; 120 minutes/month; 3 minutes per recording; 50 uploads, 10 AI summaries, 1,000 Brain credits, 4 bilingual uses, and 2 monolingual translation uses per month.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual advertised 40% off); 7-day Business trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: Transcription minutes do not carry over. On downgrade, old transcripts remain stored but a Free user can view only the first 3 minutes. Translation and Brain capacity above the included quotas require separately priced add-ons.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Notta, transcribe uploaded or live audio, summarize it, and organize a personal archive. The hard boundary is mobile apps, cloud sync, language coverage, meeting bots, and exports, plus capture reliability, integrations, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Record or import audio, transcribe it locally, identify speakers with manual correction, generate structured summaries, and organize a personal archive.
requirements: optional OpenAI or Anthropic API key
whatYouLose: mobile apps, cloud sync, language coverage, meeting bots, and exports
ongoingBurden: audio permissions, model updates, calendar APIs, storage, speaker correction, and sync
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Notta because a meeting tool must capture every call without surprising anyone, then make the result searchable and shareable across a team. The recurring cost buys audio permissions, model updates, calendar APIs, storage, speaker correction, and sync, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: whisper.cpp
priorArt.desc: Widely used local Whisper inference implementation suitable for private transcription.

alternatives.name: Buzz
alternatives.desc: Offline file and live transcription with speaker labels, search, exports and an optional summary plugin.

facts.install: macOS DMG or Windows installer from SourceForge; Flatpak/Snap on Linux; PyPI is an alternative
facts.engines: OpenAI Whisper through several local backends including whisper.cpp and Hugging Face-compatible Whisper models, with CUDA, Apple Silicon and Vulkan acceleration; optional plugins add AI summaries
facts.dataFormat: Input media and exported TXT/SRT/VTT files remain on the computer; downloaded models, application state, logs and transcription workspace data live in the platform's local Buzz cache/config directories
facts.gapVsPaid: It transcribes files and live audio very well, but lacks Notta's hosted multi-device archive, mobile/web collaboration, meeting integrations and turnkey sharing.
facts.setupBlocker: The Windows installer is unsigned and triggers a warning; the first model download can be large, and the PyPI route additionally needs Python 3.12 and ffmpeg

alternatives.name: Meetily
alternatives.desc: Local live transcription, imported recordings and summaries for Mac and Windows.

facts.install: Signed Windows x64 installer or Apple-silicon macOS DMG; Linux currently requires a source build
facts.engines: Local Whisper or NVIDIA Parakeet for transcription; local Ollama or the built-in summarizer, with Claude, OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter and custom OpenAI-compatible summary providers depending on edition
facts.dataFormat: Transcription models, recordings, transcripts and application data stay on the local machine; the Community Edition has no cloud sync
facts.gapVsPaid: It keeps meetings local but is not a full Notta-style web/mobile workspace; collaboration, broad import automation, translation workflow and several advanced outputs are weaker or Pro-only.
facts.setupBlocker: Windows and Apple-silicon macOS install cleanly but still need audio permissions and model downloads; Linux requires Rust/Node source-build tooling, and several advanced summary/export/diarization workflows are Pro-only

alternatives.name: Muesli
alternatives.desc: Live meeting capture and file import with local transcription, notes and history; Mac only.

facts.install: Signed macOS DMG or Homebrew cask
facts.engines: Parakeet TDT, Nemotron 3.5, Cohere Transcribe, Qwen3 ASR, SenseVoice, IndicConformer, experimental Gemma ASR, or WhisperKit locally; Silero VAD and FluidAudio/pyannote diarization; OpenAI, OpenRouter, ChatGPT OAuth, Ollama, LM Studio, or a custom LLM for notes
facts.dataFormat: Meeting history, transcripts, notes and settings live in a local SQLite database at ~/Library/Application Support/Muesli/muesli.db; captured audio and app-support files remain on the Mac, with optional text-only iCloud/CloudKit sync
facts.gapVsPaid: It is Mac-only and local-first, giving up Notta's broad web/mobile access, team spaces, managed sharing, integrations and cross-device archive.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14.2+, microphone/accessibility/system-audio permissions, and a first model download; cloud summaries need an account or API key unless you configure Ollama or LM Studio

alternatives.name: OpenWhispr
alternatives.desc: Records meetings or imports audio, labels speakers, summarizes it and keeps a searchable archive.

facts.install: Native DMG, EXE, AppImage, DEB or RPM; optional OpenWhispr Cloud account
facts.engines: Local Whisper/whisper.cpp or NVIDIA Parakeet via sherpa-onnx; local llama.cpp models or cloud/BYOK providers including OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Groq, Tinfoil and OpenRouter
facts.dataFormat: Transcriptions and notes live in a local SQLite database; optional retained audio stays on-device, and optional Cloud Sync stores notes and agent conversations in Neon while raw audio and standalone transcriptions do not sync
facts.gapVsPaid: It offers local recording and notes, but Notta has a more mature hosted archive, mobile/web collaboration, import connectors and translation workflow; some OpenWhispr sync and meeting features are paid.
facts.setupBlocker: The installer is straightforward, but meeting capture needs microphone/accessibility and sometimes system-audio permissions plus model downloads; cloud processing, sharing and sync require an account or provider key and some meeting features are paid

alternatives.name: Speakr
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted archive for recordings, transcripts, summaries and search; bring a server and preferably a GPU.

facts.install: Docker Compose with an environment file, plus a speech-to-text and text-model endpoint
facts.engines: Self-hosted WhisperX or compatible ASR; OpenAI transcription, Mistral/Voxtral, AssemblyAI and other connector backends; OpenAI/OpenRouter-compatible or local LLMs for summaries, chat and embeddings
facts.dataFormat: Audio lives on the server filesystem by default or S3-compatible object storage; recordings, transcripts, summaries, users, tags and search metadata live in SQLite by default or PostgreSQL
facts.gapVsPaid: It can become a capable private archive, but requires server and model administration and is less turnkey than Notta's hosted upload, live transcription, collaboration and mobile access.
facts.setupBlocker: You need Docker, API keys or a separately deployed ASR/LLM service, and a virtual audio device such as BlackHole or VB-Cable to capture both sides of some meetings; the strongest diarization path benefits from a GPU

alternatives.name: Vibe
alternatives.desc: A desktop transcriber with file batches, live capture, translation and optional local summaries; collaboration is now a folder.

facts.install: Native desktop download for macOS, Windows or Linux
facts.engines: Whisper/whisper.cpp, NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 or Parakeet TDT v3 locally with CoreML or Vulkan acceleration; optional Claude API summaries or local Ollama analysis
facts.dataFormat: Source media, downloaded model files and app configuration stay on the device; transcripts are exported locally as SRT, VTT, TXT, HTML, PDF, JSON or DOCX
facts.gapVsPaid: It is an excellent local desktop transcriber, but its 'archive' is ordinary files rather than Notta's searchable, synchronized web/mobile workspace with sharing and team collaboration.
facts.setupBlocker: Expect a sizeable first model download and local CPU/GPU/RAM demands; Claude summaries need an API key and local summaries require a running Ollama model

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal meeting notebook DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Notta in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, whisper.cpp, and a minimal HTMX interface; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: record or import audio, transcribe it locally, identify speakers with manual correction, generate structured summaries, and organize a personal archive.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Add explicit start, pause, resume, and stop controls with a visible recording indicator.
Support importing WAV, MP3, M4A, and MP4 files through ffmpeg.
Run transcription locally and display timestamped editable segments.
Let the user rename speakers and propagate corrections through the transcript.
Generate decisions, action items, questions, and a concise summary from approved text.
Export Markdown, plain text, and WebVTT beside the original recording.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out silent background capture.
Deliberately leave out automatic bot attendance in video meetings.
Deliberately leave out team workspaces and enterprise retention controls.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
